extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for DFG individual research grants and reviewers/committee members involved in DFG proposal assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how DFG (Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft) evaluates individual research grant proposals, including core evaluation criteria, standard evaluation dimensions, special considerations, and procedural aspects of review and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG funding proposals are assessed based on scientifically relevant criteria alone, including scientific excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of DFG's core evaluation criteria; reviewers assess proposals on a voluntary basis with scientific excellence as a primary consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance is one of the core criteria used to assess funding proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators judge how the proposal relates to current research questions and the degree to which it addresses important scientific problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality is a core evaluation criterion for DFG proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment includes the novelty of ideas and approaches relative to existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality and originality of the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard evaluation dimension: 'Scientific quality and originality' of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors evaluate the overall scientific merit and novelty of the project as a central dimension in comparing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to current research questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard evaluation dimension: 'Relevance' — how the project relates to current research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider the fit of the project within current disciplinary or interdisciplinary agendas and its potential to advance understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological approach and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard evaluation dimension: 'Methodological approach and feasibility'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the proposed methods are appropriate, rigorous, and feasible given the project's aims and resources; feasibility includes timelines and practical implementation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and expertise of the applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard evaluation dimension: 'Qualifications and expertise of the applicants'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on whether applicants possess the specialist knowledge and skills necessary to carry out the project; reviewers are selected based on specialist expertise to judge this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record (publications, projects, research environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard evaluation dimension: 'Track record' including publications, projects, and research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider past research achievements, relevant outputs, and whether the host environment/institution supports the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation plans (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard evaluation dimension: 'Cooperation' plans, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project involves collaborations, reviewers examine the clarity, appropriateness, and added value of proposed cooperation and roles of partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment and contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard evaluation dimension: 'Risk assessment' and contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should identify potential risks to project success and present plausible mitigation or contingency measures; reviewers assess realism and adequacy of these plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and diversity (in coordinated programmes)
rubrics_metrics.description: In DFG's coordinated programmes, equity and diversity in research are relevant to the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, assessment includes consideration of equity and diversity aspects; this is an explicit additional consideration for coordinated programmes rather than a universal evaluation metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career circumstances (favourable consideration of special/unavoidable circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any special and unavoidable personal circumstances pertaining to an applicant are taken into account exclusively in their favour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: periods of childcare, absence due to health, care of family members, and other documented circumstances. Applicants supply these details voluntarily; reviewers/boards must consider them to the applicant's advantage when evaluating qualifications and track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science and data practices (DORA-aligned)
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG emphasizes open data, reproducibility, and research assessment aligned with DORA: no reliance on journal impact factors; quality of research over quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should not use journal impact factors as a proxy for quality. Proposals are expected to consider open data and reproducibility practices; assessment favors transparent, reproducible research and appropriate data sharing plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-stage evaluation process (review, assessment, decision) and separation of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG uses a three-stage process: Stage 1 Review (independent assessments by specialist reviewers), Stage 2 Assessment (review boards evaluate reviews and apply standardized criteria), Stage 3 Decision (Joint Committee/Senate makes final funding decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation of review, evaluation, and decision functions is intended to ensure professional and fair assessment. Approximately 17,000 reviewers are consulted annually and are selected based on specialist expertise; review boards apply standardized assessment criteria across proposals; final funding decisions rest with governing committees.
